description: DistributedTraining Operator — lifecycle, solver accuracy, and training results

panels.title: Time Prediction Error % (− = faster than predicted)
panels.description: Signed prediction error: 100 × (actual − predicted) / predicted. Negative = actual finished faster than predicted (green, solver was conservative); positive = actual ran slower than predicted (red, solver was optimistic / promise missed).

panels.title: Scaling overhead α — convergence across runs
panels.description: Latest α value across all selected runs at each timestamp. Each step corresponds to a new solver invocation incorporating a fresh history entry. A flattening step pattern indicates convergence: α is stabilizing as more data accumulates.

Final training loss per run (eval_loss, falling back to train_loss). Lower is better. Operator runs emit this from collected job logs; baselines are pushed via Pushgateway. Compares the selected runs ($dj_name).
panels.title: Loss per Run
Pod Runtime (s) — Baseline vs Operator at same N
panels.description: Multi-select baseline-b-2/3 and distributedtraining-cal-2node/3node to compare pod runtime at matched node counts. Operator and baseline use the same training_seconds window (PyTorchJob status.startTime → completionTime).
From transfer_profile.json. compute + dataload ≈ 1 at one node. AllReduce is the union of in-flight AllReduce intervals — an upper bound, DDP overlaps it with backward.
panels.title: Transfer fractions per run — share of the measured step time

panels.description: Ring-estimate wire bytes (2(n−1)/n × reduced) ÷ AllReduce time. 0 at one node.
panels.title: AllReduce bandwidth per run

panels.description: nfs_read_bytes ÷ data-load time, rank 0's process tree. 0 for synthetic runs or page-cache hits.
panels.title: NFS read bandwidth per run

panels.description: Same rule as the operator's classifier (phases.go classifyBottleneck): compute ≥ 0.6 → compute-bound; else AllReduce ≥ data-load → communication-bound; else data-bound. The operator's own verdict is in the CR status.results.bottleneck and the Bottleneck event.
panels.title: Bottleneck class per run

panels.description: The gap between the two is the serial remainder inside the training window (model load, eval, save).
panels.title: Throughput per run: wall-clock (W ÷ training s, what the solver fits) vs inner loop

panels.description: Divide by the 1-node value of the same series to get η(n); α = (1−η)/(η(n−1)).
panels.title: Per-node wall-clock throughput (scaling efficiency proxy)

panels.description: One row per run (latest values). Columns F–H (fractions) against E (α) give the scaling-explanation relationship.
panels.title: Per-run scaling summary

panels.description: exp(eval_loss) on the validation/test split. With fixed total work, more nodes = fewer optimizer steps at a larger effective batch — expect a small drift.
panels.title: Perplexity per run (held-out eval)

panels.description: Number of CRs (matching the filters) that ever reached each phase. Counts series rather than counter increases so it also works for replayed data, where counters never move.
panels.title: Runs reaching Succeeded / Failed
